title: Cap. VI Arg. 9: first — Christ the Mediator predestined without prior merits (Augustine)
pass_a_gloss: As to the former: If it be asked, How was Christ predestinated to be Savior? according to the gratuitous good pleasure of God, or according to foresight of works? hear the same Augustine: There is also a most illustrious light of predestination and grace, the Savior himself, the Mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus: who, that he might be this, by what preceding merits of his own, whether of works or of faith, did the human nature which is in him procure it? On the Predestination of the Saints, chapter 15.
pass_b_english: First limb: how was Christ predestined Savior — by God's gratuitous good pleasure, or by foresight of works? Hear Augustine (On the Predestination of the Saints 15): the brightest light of predestination and grace is the Savior himself, the Mediator, the man Christ Jesus — and by what prior merits of his own, of works or of faith, did the human nature in him earn to be that?
source_text: Quod ad prius: Si quaeratur, Quomodo Christus in Salvatorem praedestinatus? secundum Dei gratuitum beneplacitum, an secundum praevisionem operum? audite eundem Augustinum: Est etiam praeclarissimum lumen praedestinationis et gratiae ipse Salvator, ipse Mediator Dei et hominum, homo Christus Jesus: qui ut hoc esset, quibus tandem suis, vel operum vel fidei, praecedentibus meritis naturae humanae quae in illo est comparavit? De Praed. Sanct. cap. 15.
